title: Attribution Studio: per-token breakdown, export flows, and pricing pattern proposals
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and prototype a compact "Attribution Studio" for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-token cost breakdowns, supports flexible attribution rules (prompt vs completion, system messages, function calls), and provides export flows (CSV/Parquet) plus a pricing-pattern composer for billing simulations. The goal is to provide clear unit economics at the route/model/prompt-set level while keeping export performance and privacy controls in mind.
background: Customers asked for more explainability around surges in spend and for an easy way to export token-level ledgers to downstream chargeback systems. Existing Console screens show aggregate token spend but lack an interactive composer for attribution rules or a performant export path for high-cardinality billing exports. This ticket consolidates design work: interactive breakdown UI, attribution rule editor, export UX, and a small set of pricing UI patterns that can be reused in Console billing and Dedicated onboarding flows.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to filter token spend by route and model so I can reconcile spikes with deployments.
As a finance analyst, I want to export a per-request token ledger (CSV/Parquet) with applied pricing so I can import into our chargeback system.
As a PM, I want to prototype pricing slabs and see cost previews so I can validate commercial impact of new SKUs.
As a security officer, I want RBAC and PII redaction options for exports so we meet compliance requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Attribution Studio prototype in Figma with screens for: breakdown overview, rule editor, export settings, and pricing-slab composer.
Export options include CSV and Parquet; demonstration export of 100k rows (sample dataset) completes within prototype performance budget for user testing.
Attribution rules include at minimum: token type (prompt/completion), message role (system/user/assistant), model variant mapping, and custom weights; UI shows immediate cost preview.
Pricing pattern composer supports fixed-per-token, tiered slabs, and blended overrides; preview shows dollar impact for a selected time window.
Design review notes addressed and handoff artifacts (redlines, copy, accessibility checklist) uploaded to Confluence and Figma.
Privacy and export controls documented: RBAC gating, pseudonymization toggle, and required legal/CS approvals for customer exports.
design_notes: Prefer a compact 'studio' modal pattern to avoid full-page displacement; allow deep-linking to model/route context from Console charts.
Primary breakdown visual: stacked waterfall showing token categories (prompt, completion, system, tool-call), cost per token, and top contributing routes.
Introduce a rule editor that compiles to deterministic transformations applied server-side for export — provide human-readable summary and JSON preview for engineers.
Export pagination and chunking UX: show estimated file count and suggested compressed output for >500k rows; expose background export with email/webhook completion.
Pricing pattern builder UX: 'Quick presets' for common SaaS patterns and an 'Advanced mode' for composing hybrid slabs and rounding rules.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Cho): prefer explicit separation of 'preview' and 'apply' — users should be able to simulate pricing without altering backend state.
Eng (Marco Diaz): backend will only accept rule sets under 16KB; recommend limiting free-text conditions and offering a library of precompiled rules.
Security (Priya Raman): exports containing request metadata require PII redaction flag; add a mandatory confirmation step for exports >90 days of data.
Design lead (Sofia Nguyen): suggest stronger affordance for 'reasoning trace' — show the rule path that attributed tokens to a SKU for auditability.
decisions: Modal-first studio chosen to enable context-preserving workflow and quick experiments.
Export will support background processing and webhook notifications for large jobs; initial implementation will provide CSV and Parquet only.
Pricing patterns: ship three presets (flat per-token, tiered slabs, blended override) and postpone custom function formulas to a future iteration.
Attribution rules will be compiled server-side; UI will provide a JSON export of the compiled rule for infra engineers.
next_steps: Finalize Figma prototype addressing review feedback (owner: Noah) — due 2025-03-08.
Schedule design-review with Eng and Security for API contract and export throttling (owner: Ava) — target 2025-03-10.
Run 2 moderated usability sessions with finance and platform users using sample exports (owner: UX Research) — target complete by 2025-03-15.
Create frontend spike ticket for modal integration and background export UX (link to ENG ticket after review).
